mentions.name: Duckies AI
mentions.description: This is an AI-enhanced IDE with mentor/skill-level awareness baked in, combining rubber-ducking and mob programming. It features 'Duckies' with distinct personalities (skills) that each specialize in a particular kind of problem, 'teachable moments' bubbles that surface novel, tangential, or foundational information while you work, and skill-level detection with a routing model so it doesn't overwhelm users with unneeded explanations. Each duck runs on a tiered memory model rather than a flat context window: core memory defining its skills, long-term memory for company standards and code style, a separate project-scoped long-term memory, and short-term memory for the current task, so ducks reason like team members with real employment history rather than chatbots.
mentions.problem: Juniors and new hires often fall into an impostor-syndrome trap when reading an unfamiliar codebase or reviewing a senior peer's PR; documentation usually runs into the curse of knowledge, written by people who have lost sight of what it's like to be new to the codebase.
mentions.audience: Juniors and new hires who struggle with impostor syndrome when reading unfamiliar codebases or reviewing senior peers' PRs, and for whom documentation suffers from the curse of knowledge.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm slowly building an IDE with mentor/skill-level awareness baked in.
mentions.author: bryanculver
